code.text: Chest X-ray, posteroanterior and lateral: lungs clear and not hyperinflated; no consolidation, hilar enlargement, cavity, scarring or effusion; heart size normal

Reversible airflow obstruction: asthma

Written asthma action plan, given and explained: green zone use the reliever as needed; yellow zone (more symptoms, waking, or peak flow below 80 percent of her best) use more reliever inhalations up to 12 a day and call the clinic; red zone (peak flow below 50 percent, cannot speak in sentences, or no relief) emergency care. Asthma action plan updated for travel: peak flow zones set from her personal best of 400 L/min (green above 320, yellow 200 to 320, red below 200); instructions for the standby prednisone course and for finding care at sea and abroad; a printed medical summary

text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Pulmonology consultation in two weeks with spirometry before and after bronchodilator and FeNO, to confirm or refute asthma, exclude other chest disease, and plan treatment and preparation for travel
  • Work-up of wheeze and cough: chest X-ray, blood count with eosinophils, interferon-gamma release assay for tuberculosis infection (born in a country where tuberculosis is common), and a urine pregnancy test before treatment; no inhaler is started before testing unless symptoms worsen
  • Trauma-informed, patient-centred care: seen alone for part of every visit; consent, information and results to her alone, through her own contact details; no instructions about her care accepted from the household; private screening for safety and exploitation at each visit, with resources and social work offered and her decisions respected
  • Equity safeguards: spirometry read with race-neutral GLI Global equations, plain explanation of every result, and attention to the higher asthma burden carried by Black women
  • GINA track 1, step 2: as-needed low-dose budesonide-formoterol (no albuterol-only reliever), a written action plan with peak flow zones, technique checks and trigger reduction (kitchen ventilation, avoiding fireplace smoke, a scarf in cold wind, mite-proof bedding); review six weeks after starting and within a week of any exacerbation
  • Vaccines for an adult with asthma: influenza and COVID-19 each season, and PCV20 once
  • Travel plan for a long sea journey: two inhalers and a spacer, an updated action plan, a standby five-day prednisone course with clear start rules, meclizine for seasickness, an aired cabin away from smoke, a printed medical summary and contact with the clinic by message
  • Contraception and pregnancy planning on her terms: information on every method (all suitable with asthma), folic acid 0.4 mg daily by her choice, and asthma review before and during any pregnancy with budesonide as the preferred inhaled steroid and the controller never stopped
  • After the exacerbation: GINA track 1 step 3, budesonide-formoterol one inhalation twice daily and as needed through the winter, with a step-down to as-needed treatment in the spring if she stays well
  • Social work, at her request, for health coverage in her own name, income and housing after she gained her freedom

resource.title: Phillis Wheatley synthetic care plan
resource.description: Confirm asthma in a 19-year-old Black woman, born in West Africa, who has been called frail and asthmatic since childhood but never tested: spirometry with bronchodilator response read with race-neutral equations, FeNO and blood eosinophils, with tuberculosis excluded. Then treat on GINA 1772 track 1 (as-needed low-dose budesonide-formoterol, stepping to maintenance-and-reliever therapy after an exacerbation), write an action plan, address her triggers (cold air, cooking and fireplace smoke, colds), prepare her for a long sea journey and a summer away from her clinic, vaccinate, screen for depression and anxiety, and counsel on contraception and pregnancy planning with asthma (budesonide preferred, controller continued in pregnancy). Her social history at the true-frame index date is enslavement: the modern episode renders it truthfully as domestic servitude, and the clinic practises trauma-informed, patient-centred care in which she alone consents, decides and receives her information.
